results.title: How Revolut Cut AI Coding Costs 90% With Self-Hosted Open Models - David Abitbol, Revolut｜AI Engineer — BigGo Finance
results.content:
Revolut's data comes from a sample of 2,000 engineers tracked over roughly a year. The first AI rollout, Gemini in January 2025, produced a 10% improvement in lead time and 20% in coding time — Abitbol attributes the coding gain to engineers no longer digging through Stack Overflow and documentation. Claude Code, trialed around February 2025 and launched at scale in January 2026, showed little measurable impact at first, and Revolut was skeptical of the cost: engineers were spending $1,000 to $10,000 a month with weak ROI, so the rollout came with strict budget limits. [...] ## Long context is a trap and FP4 is the floor

Abitbol lists the parameters that matter, and leads with a contrarian one: long context is "a scam." Even if a model can serve one million tokens, 256K is what the workload actually needs. On quantization, Blackwell-generation GPUs should run nothing higher than FP4 — moving from FP4 to FP8 costs roughly 40% more GPU footprint for zero precision gain, by his account.

The rest of the checklist:

 Tensor parallelism: GLM fits on TP4, but KV cache runs short; TP8 may serve better depending on workload size.
 Cache hit rate: coding tasks need above 90%.
 Advanced techniques: optimized speculative decoding, sequential pre-fill, and PD (prefill-decode) disaggregation.
